blocks.html: This chapter applies the regression and testing toolkit of Chapters 8–14 to problems a community-medicine researcher meets again and again: choosing a model (§15.1), clustered and survey data (§15.2), confounding in observational comparisons (§15.3), missing values (§15.4), diagnostic tests and prediction models (§15.5), sample size (§15.6), meta-analysis (§15.7), Bayesian reasoning (§15.8) and randomised trials (§15.9). The sections are largely independent; each names the earlier sections it builds on. The running example is again the CBHI survey: 500 households in 20 villages, 25 per village, with 30% (150/500) CBHI members.
